findings.problem: status is a raw String; any arbitrary string value ("sent", "", "cancelled", "foo") is a valid BudgetWorkflow, violating the typestate guarantee that status transitions are enforced by the compiler.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can set status to any string, creating illegal states that no runtime check can prevent; downstream code cannot pattern-match on status at the type level.
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with `pub status: BudgetStatus` where `BudgetStatus` is an enum (e.g., `Draft`, `Validated`, `Sent`) and remove the separate `is_sent` flag.

findings.problem: is_validated and is_sent are independent bool flags that can represent logically impossible combinations (validated=true, sent=false, sent=true, validated=false — i.e., a sent budget that was never validated).
findings.failure_mode: A budget can reach the state {is_validated: true, is_sent: false} or {is_validated: false, is_sent: true}, both of which violate the domain invariant that sent budgets must first be validated. Runtime checks on two independent booleans cannot prevent these illegal states at compile time.
findings.fix: Replace both bool fields with a single typestate enum (e.g., `BudgetState { Draft, Validated, Sent { sent_at: Timestamp } }`) so illegal states are unrepresentable.

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts any BudgetWorkflow and unconditionally marks it as sent, with no check that is_validated is true before allowing the transition. The name implies a workflow precondition (validated first) that is not enforced in code.
findings.failure_mode: An invalid/unvalidated budget can be marked as sent, bypassing the validation gate and allowing unvalidated budgets into downstream systems. This is a data-integrity violation at the domain boundary.
findings.fix: Change the signature to accept a `ValidatedBudget` (newtype wrapping BudgetWorkflow with validated=true) or return a Result, requiring the caller to prove validation before calling mark_sent. Alternatively, use a typestate enum and only accept the Validated variant in a `transition_to_sent` method.

findings.problem: All fields of BudgetWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to mutate status, is_validated, and is_sent directly without going through any domain method or transition function.
findings.failure_mode: External callers can set is_sent = true without invoking mark_sent, completely bypassing the (already weak) lifecycle logic. Public mutable fields are an encapsulation breach.
findings.fix: Make all fields private and provide only domain methods (e.g., `new()`, `validate()`, `mark_sent()`) or constructors for each valid state variant.

findings.problem: id is a raw String with no domain constraints or newtype wrapper. Any string is accepted as a budget ID.
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, malformed IDs, or IDs from unrelated domains can be used interchangeably, risking ID collisions and comparison mistakes with other String IDs in the system.
findings.fix: Introduce `pub struct BudgetId(String)` with a fallible constructor that enforces domain constraints (non-empty, valid format), and use `BudgetId` as the field type.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is Option<u64>, a raw epoch-ms value with no newtype or timezone/semantics annotation. No checked arithmetic or conversion guards are present.
findings.failure_mode: Consumers may interpret this as a different time unit, overflow when converting to other types, or treat year-2038 values incorrectly. Without a typed wrapper, domain semantics are lost.
findings.fix: Introduce `pub struct SentAtEpochMs(u64)` and use it as the field type. Provide `TryFrom` impls for safe conversions and document the epoch-ms contract.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes `mut item: BudgetWorkflow` by value and returns `BudgetWorkflow`, mutating the input in place and returning the whole struct. This is a command-style mutation, not a pure functional-core pattern.
findings.failure_mode: Callers may reuse the original binding thinking it was immutable; the mutation happens on the parameter and the caller must use the return value. Pure functions would take an immutable reference or a constructor-style API.
findings.fix: Either accept `&BudgetWorkflow` and return a new `BudgetWorkflow` / `BudgetState::Sent` variant, or use a builder/constructor pattern that produces a new typed value instead of mutating in place.

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The code is structurally deficient in type safety: illegal states are fully representable, validation preconditions are not enforced, and mark_sent bypasses the domain workflow. Without enum-based typestates and a validated-only constructor for mark_sent, the crate cannot prevent unvalidated budgets from being marked as sent.
